# OpenProgram 0.8.3 Release Notes

OpenProgram 0.8.3 improves long conversation loading and isolates browser previews by conversation.

## 🐞 Bug fixes

- Packaged-runtime verification supports the system Bash 3.2 on macOS without weakening browser verification.

- Browser previews stay bound to their actual conversation. Private pages require trusted ownership until explicitly revealed as a standalone tab.
- Long graph traversal no longer fails at Python's recursion limit.

## ✨ New features

- Load earlier messages on demand while preserving branch identity and live message ordering.

## 🚀 Improvements

- Large history and graph responses use bounded WebSocket fragments without increasing the 4 MiB sender queue.
- Session and branch loading move expensive projection work off the WebSocket event loop and avoid repeated ancestor scans.

## 📦 Download and installation

- **macOS**
  - **Package installation**
    - Apple Silicon: download `OpenProgram-0.8.3-mac-arm64-unsigned.dmg` or `OpenProgram-0.8.3-mac-arm64-unsigned.zip`.
    - Intel: download `OpenProgram-0.8.3-mac-x64-unsigned.dmg` or `OpenProgram-0.8.3-mac-x64-unsigned.zip`.
  - **Command-line installation**
    - Run `curl -fsSL https://openprogram.io/install | sh`.
  - **Development installation**
    - Follow the development installation guide for source editing and testing.
  - macOS package and command-line installations share the same complete runtime and browser backend. Electron multi-Pane support and the built-in Browser Pane are available only in the macOS Desktop App.
- **Linux**
  - **Command-line / Server installation**
    - Run `curl -fsSL https://openprogram.io/install | sh`.
  - **Development installation**
    - Follow the development installation guide for source editing and testing.

## 🔄 Upgrade guide

- Desktop users can install the matching DMG and replace the existing application.
- CLI and Server users can run `openprogram upgrade` or repeat the public installation command.
- User data under `~/.openprogram` is preserved.

The release also includes Python wheel and source-distribution artifacts, complete managed runtimes for supported macOS and Linux architectures, checksums, and a machine-readable release manifest.

Stored history and model context compaction are unchanged. Full graph construction and initial session indexing still use resources proportional to session size.
